# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `cursor_file.rs` — the cursor file, format v1 (road map "creator-jobs" CU1a, spec
  §11 CU-10): its module doc IS the format's specification (the header, the columns
  in integer µs and points × 100, the caps, every refusal's sentence, the parse
  order); `RC_CURSOR_FILE_VERSION` (the header's `#define` held to it by
  `core/tests/cursor_file.rs`), the caps, the types and `CursorFile::parse`, which
  reads the object, `format`, `version` and CU-7's `typed` keys loosely BEFORE the
  strict `deny_unknown_fields` read through `serde_path_to_error`, so a newer file is
  refused by its version and a project by its format. `cursor_file_check.rs` — its
  check (`check`, `check_typed`; a shortcut holds `cmd` or `ctrl`, or `opt` with
  `OPTION_SHORTCUT_KEYS`, CU-60) and the base64 decoder, a module of its own because
  the two together pass the 400-line cap for a new file. `ffi_cursor.rs` —
  `rc_cursor_open` (parse and check; an open is the recorder's read-back, CU-15),
  `rc_cursor_free` and `rc_cursor_query` (road map creator-jobs CU2, spec §11 CU-25).
  `cursor_track.rs` — `CursorTrack`, the handle: the parsed file and its prepared
  paths under a `Mutex` (a `state` holds it only to clone an `Arc`, a poisoned lock
  taken with `into_inner`), ticks ↔ µs through `time.rs`, CU-20's M2 mapping per
  geometry entry (`scale_factor`, not `pixels_per_point`; `to_movie`, the one function), the raw path, idle opacity (CU-22),
  the image in force and ripples (CU-23). `cursor_smooth.rs` — `hold_end`, the one
  hold rule, and `SmoothPath` (pins, RDP, centripetal Catmull–Rom; CU-21).
  `cursor_query.rs` — the request vocabulary (its module doc) and `query`.
  `cursor_query_reads.rs` — its `events` and `path` reads, a pure move out of it (road map
  creator-jobs CU11a's toll); `state` takes `ends` and answers the shutter's two positions (spec
  §11 CU-115).
  `cursor_bursts.rs` — typing stretches and scroll bursts, one run finder. Auto Zoom's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU7, spec §11 CU-70…CU-75), `plan_zooms` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_zoom.rs` its
  arguments, refusals in CU-75's order, Replace's removals (`is_zoom` only), the bases a
  hold across a cut sets, and the ops (`remove_action`, `set_video`, `add_zoom_action` in
  time order) and answer; `cursor_zoom_run.rs` a run (clips continuing one source on one
  track) — its anchors through S, scroll bursts, barriers, the 10 Hz follow cursor and
  `land` (only given clips, no straddled cut); `cursor_zoom_visits.rs` anchors → visits →
  planned actions in container time, pure. Add Shortcut Overlays' planner (road map
  creator-jobs CU8, spec §11 CU-80…CU-84), `plan_overlays` in `rc_cursor_query` (one track per
  clip, and the project): `cursor_overlays.rs` — its arguments and refusals, the presses through
  `cursor_zoom_run.rs`'s `media_in` and `clip_time`, CU-80's timing in grid frames
  (`min_frames`, D_min(n) = 10n + 25; the same chord merged as "×k"; a different chord more than
  0.5 s late dropped), CU-83's Shortcuts track rule (`TRACK_NAME`; the front-most one in front of
  every given clip's track, unlocked, shown, no matte, free over the span, else a new one at the
  front with `next_id`) and the `add_track` / `add_graphic_clip` ops. Speed Up Typing's
  planner (road map creator-jobs CU9b, spec §11 CU-91, CU-92), `plan_typing` in
  `rc_cursor_query` (one track per clip, and the project): `cursor_typing.rs` — its arguments
  and refusals (rate ×2–×8, shortest 1–30 s, then per clip; reversed refused), each typing
  stretch clamped to the played window through `clip_time`, less every speech span of a media
  clip with sound under it (`speech_in_clip`) and each recorded press's overlay span
  (Shortcuts-track clips holding it or starting within `MOST_LATE`, else `DEFAULT_DURATION`,
  both `cursor_overlays.rs`'s; presses not filtered by `[from, to)`), every clip's pieces
  united (touching merged) before `shortest` and the 0.3 s margins, `needs_speech` when a
  counted media has no `speech`, and the `retime_range` ops right to left, tried in order on a
  clone (all or nothing). `encode_base64`
  sits beside `decode_base64` in `cursor_file_check.rs`, base64's one home. No file
  I/O, no pixel work: a PNG is checked by its signature.
- `model_cursor.rs` · `cursor_props.rs` · `recipe_cursor.rs` — the cursor in the model and the
  recipe (format 38, road map "creator-jobs" CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-32, CU-35, CU-39):
  `model_cursor.rs` `MediaCursor` (`media.cursor`, after `speech`, written only when set,
  `in_picture` required) and `CursorProps` (`video.cursor`, after `look`, written only when set,
  every field written, `{}` the defaults) with `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` and the `CURSOR_*`
  ranges, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; `cursor_props.rs` `check_cursor` (one line in
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_video`), `clamp_cursor` (one line in `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_video`; it never fails, so the video group always decodes), `check_media_cursor`
  (`check_media_fields`' last check) and `with_base_cursor`, the one statement that `smoothing`
  and `hide_idle` are the clip's BASE values — read by `recipe_cursor.rs`, `edit_split.rs`'s
  second half and `freeze_frame`'s still; `recipe_cursor.rs` `Project::layer_cursor`, a layer's
  `cursor` key: `null` unless a media or still clip's media has a cursor not `in_picture` and the
  evaluated props show or ripple, else `{media, at, reversed, smoothing, hide_idle, props}`, `at`
  `freeze_frame`'s source tick in the stream the clip plays.
- `model_cutout.rs` · `cutout_check.rs` — the cutout in the model (format 39, road map
  "creator-jobs" CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21, CO-23): `model_cutout.rs` `Cutout`
  (`video.cutout`, after `cursor`, written only when set, every field written, `{}` the
  defaults) with `CutoutSubject` (`person`, and `foreground`, format 41, road map creator-jobs
  CO10a, spec §11 CO-100), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground` and the `CUTOUT_*` ranges,
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; `cutout_check.rs` `check_cutout` (one line in
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_video`: edge, feather, then `best` refused), `check_cutout_clip` (one
  line in `edit_props.rs`'s `settle_video`: a media, still or image clip takes one, a text, shape,
  graphic, adjustment or nest clip refused naming what it is, then `foreground` refused on a media
  or still clip in its own sentence, CO-100), `check_behind_subject_clip` (one line in `settle_video` after it:
  `video.behind_subject`, format 40, spec §11 CO-52, refused on an adjustment or nest clip),
  `clamp_cutout` (one line in `actions_clamp.rs`'s `clamp_video`; it
  never fails) and `restore_base_cutout` (through `restore_base_video_keys`, one line in
  `actions.rs`'s `evaluate_clip`, beside motion's restore: the presence, `subject` and `quality`
  the base's). The recipe's `cutout` key
  is `recipe_layer.rs`'s `Project::layer_cutout`: `null` unless a media, still or image clip's media
  is in the project and the evaluated cutout is set, else `{mask: {kind: "media", media, quality},
  background, edge, feather}`, `media` the clip's own source media; an image clip's mask is
  `{kind: "image", media, subject, quality}` (CO-101), drawn uncut until CO10b. `add_blurred_background`'s
  copy drops it. `VideoProps.behind_subject` (format 40, after `cutout`, written only when true)
  is `model_props.rs`'s; the copy drops it too. `cutout_check.rs` also holds hide while
  silent's checks (format 43, spec §11 CO-92): `check_hide_silent`,
  `Project::check_hide_silent_clip` and `restore_base_video_keys` (`video_gate.rs`'s entry).
- `motion_blur.rs` · `recipe_blur.rs` — motion blur (format 42, road map "creator-jobs"
  CU11a, spec §11 CU-110…CU-114): `motion_blur.rs` `MOTION_BLUR_SAMPLES` (CU-S5's N, 16),
  `check_motion_blur` (one line in `check_video`), `clamp_motion_blur` (one line in
  `clamp_video`), `check_motion_blur_clip` (one line in `settle_video`: a nest or adjustment
  clip refused above 0) and `shutter_offsets` (the N centred offsets and the two ends, on the
  canvas's frame); `recipe_blur.rs` `Shutter`, `Project::layer_shutter` (none at 0 or when
  `layer`'s `sharp` holds: drawn into, a matte, a transition, a dissolve, a shadow, an
  adjustment clip; times clamped into the instance's span), `Project::layer_blur` (the layer's
  `blur` key from `placement` at each time, `null` when every sample equals the first) and
  `sharpen_matted` (after `frame_subjects`: every matted layer's `blur` null and its cursor's
  `shutter` removed). `VideoProps.motion_blur` (after `behind_subject`, written only above 0)
  is `model_props.rs`'s; `video_json` always carries it; `add_blurred_background`'s copy drops
  it. `recipe_cursor.rs`'s `layer_cursor` takes the shutter's ends and appends `shutter
  {from, to, samples}`.
- `video_gate.rs` — hide while silent (format 43, road map "creator-jobs" CO9, spec §11
  CO-90…CO-93): `Project::hide_silent_gate` (an instance's gate at a tick: the nearest container,
  outward from the layer's own, in which an instance of the media covers it; there, the instances
  whose played window meets `[t − hold − fade, t + pre_roll + fade]`, each projected at its own
  origin through `audio_duck_speech.rs`'s `played_speech`, sorted and `widened`; the maximum of 1
  inside and a ramp to 0 over `fade`, a step at 0; 1 with no gate, no saved speech or no covering
  instance), multiplied into `recipe.rs`'s `layer` only (`clip_state`, `placement` and every edit
  read un-gated); `gate_entries` (the plan's `gates`, one per timeline-level gated instance, after
  `ducks`, only when non-empty, each instance's ramps windowed as the gate is); `clear_hide_silent`
  (`remove_media`'s non-LUT arm, timeline and every nest); `hide_silent_media` (paste's non-shown
  media list, `keep_range`'s kept media) and `remap_hide_silent` (an id the map lacks drops the
  gate, `remap_look_media`'s rule). `HideSilent` (`media`, `pre_roll`, `hold`, `fade`, all
  written; `HIDE_SILENT_PRE_ROLL`, `_HOLD`, `_FADE`, `_MAX`) and `VideoProps.hide_silent` (after
  `motion_blur`, written only when set) are `model_props.rs`'s; `check_hide_silent` (one line in
  `check_video`), `Project::check_hide_silent_clip` (one line in `settle_video`: media named, in
  the project, with sound, then a nest clip refused) and `restore_base_video_keys` (`actions.rs`'
  one call: the cutout's restore and the base's whole `hide_silent`) are `cutout_check.rs`'s;
  `not_a_target` refuses `video.hide_silent` in a patch and in `off`.
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its

  ignoring case, ordered, named (`Track N`, `/` and `:` as `-`, ` (Track N)`

  **Generic** — knows nothing about video; the host registers the catalog
  and a callback. Copied from Rasterize; do not add domain knowledge. Since

  `MAX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES`, 103, chmod 0600, never unlinking a file already

  packet's first byte.
- `ffi_graphic.rs` — the twelve `rc_graphic_*` exports (road map 10 §5e; the
  eleventh `rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39: set the decoded-image cache's
  limit, answer its bytes; the twelfth `rc_graphic_library_usage`, G-46: the
  font files and assets the library's draws used; two re-exported from
  `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`

  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`

- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file

governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field

  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).

- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`

  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,

- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map

  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,

  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,

  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:

  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11

  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s

- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /

  `clip`/`track`/`media`/`marker`/`nest` lookups, `clips_on`, `duration`,

  `Source::media` (the media a source reads, exhaustive over the kinds),
  `next_track_name` ("Track N" by the count), `numbered_track` (allocated
  and named, not inserted) and `remint` (a copied clip's fresh ids: the
  clip's, then each action's). The three source-window measurements moved
  out to `source_window.rs`.

  both full-paste paths and unnest. It snaps placement start, delegates the
  source-bounded duration to `source_window.rs`, clamps action spans, snaps
  present base motion/text timing through the patch snappers, and snaps a
  graphic's `in` and `length` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_resnapped` (spec §11 G-18). It does not change source positions,
  action-end payloads or audio envelopes. On a ramped clip (SR-19 (g))
  `resnap_actions` snaps the speed actions without clamping them into the
  clip (clamping would change what it reads), and `resnap_clip_times` holds
  the duration a second time over the snapped map.
- `source_window.rs` — THE source window: how much material a clip shows,
  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.
  `content_length_in_source` reads `speed_map.rs`'s map for a ramped clip
  (SR-10), so the one function still says how much source any clip reads.
  On a ramped clip (SR-18) the tail readers go through `time_for_source`,
  `in` moves by `source_read_by` / `source_advanced_through` (trims, roll,
  split, freeze), `front_edge_held` bisects the front edge to a frame that
  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
  are the fit test.

  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;
  `source_head_on_timeline`, `source_length_on_timeline` and
  `longest_duration_on_grid` — the bound, snapped DOWN (spec §11, #22) — in
  TIMELINE ticks. **Every site that WRITES a media clip's window reads the
  bound here, and which function it reads says what it writes** (spec §11,
  D4-2 to D4-5): `longest_duration_on_grid_of` is the bound from the pieces,
  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0
  and an END from the clip's own start and the two are not the same number;
  `latest_end_on_grid` and `earliest_start_on_grid` are the timeline
  POSITIONS `trim_end` / `roll` and `trim_start` / `roll` /
  `head_handle_frames` clamp to (positions, so not a `SourceBound`);
  `duration_resnapped` is what every RE-SNAP of a media duration writes
  (`resnap`, `paste` twice, `unnest`, `relink_media`'s hold to a shorter file)
  and `duration_at_speed` what

  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,
  because `None` meant "unbounded, apply no clamp" to a trim and "no handle
  at all" to a transition: the three arms are `Unbounded` (a source with no
  window), `Unmeasured` (a media window that exists and cannot be measured)
  and `Timeline`, and a caller picks what `Unmeasured` means to it BY NAME,
  `or_unbounded` or `or_empty`. `in_advanced` / `source_advanced` is the one
  `round(Δ × speed)` mover the six placement sites used to write out. Cut
  out of `model_query.rs` by road map 7 §10's phase A.

  `frames_back` (the grid position k frames before the frame nearest a
  position) and `frames_within` (the most whole frames back from a position

- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc

  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).

  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;

  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. The rows (`OP_TABLE`) and `OP_NAMES` live in

  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is

  reader is every one of the sixty-nine op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its

  `WhereEmpty` and `Subjects`, the last a caller-authored object declared
  and closed at every level; `switch_layout` added `Layout`,
  `LayoutShape`, `Corner` and `Point`, `[f64; 2]`; `Texts`, a list of strings, is

  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:

  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY

  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view

  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests

  **`tiny_http` 0.12's `Server` drop unlinks its path unconditionally (MC1's
  S7)**, so a socket listener records its file's
  device and inode as a `SocketClaim`: `shutdown` lets the drop run only
  while the claim `is_current`, and forgets the server otherwise; `release`
  (the quit path) unlinks only a current file and then forgets the whole
  listener — no unblock, no join — so a call in flight cannot hold a quit.
  The protocol revisions it negotiates are `mcp_versions.rs`'s, not its own.
- `mcp_versions.rs` — the MCP protocol revisions (`SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`,
  `LATEST_VERSION`) and `negotiate` (the requested one when supported, else
  the newest), moved out of `agent.rs` by road map 14's MC3 so ONE list
  serves two readers: `agent.rs`'s `initialize` and `mcp-proxy/`, which
  includes this file by `#[path]`. It therefore uses `std` alone and names
  nothing of this crate (no `use crate::…`).
- `ffi.rs` / `ffi_edit.rs` / `ffi_query.rs` / `ffi_agent.rs` — thin shims
  only; shared plumbing lives in `ffi_util.rs`, never copy-pasted.
  `ffi_query.rs`'s rule: a query never allocates a handle and has no
  `err_out`, which is why `rc_project_scoped` lives in `ffi.rs`.
  `rc_speed_limits` is its answer for the speed range and the audio ceiling;
  `rc_project_source_map` (`ffi_query.rs`, SR-20) a clip's source map;
  `rc_project_speaker_match` (`ffi_query.rs`, VR-65) the face-to-microphone match `follow:
  speaker` would make on a clip, for Make Vertical's sheet;
  `rc_normalise_color` (`ffi.rs`) is the colour grammar's (G-25).
  `ffi_agent.rs` has one slot, one listener per process: `SOCKET`
  (`rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`; MC4 deleted the TCP pair and its
  slot), whose `AgentConfig` is built by `host_config`, one catalog
  through one handler.
- `container.rs` · `container_header.rs` · `container_blocks.rs` ·
  `container_codec.rs` · `container_timing.rs` · `container_vorbis.rs` ·
  `container_vorbis_setup.rs` · `ffi_container.rs` — a WebM
  or Matroska file being imported, read as an INDEX (spec §11 #216-R),
  read-only, bounds-checked, no input may panic: `container_header.rs` the
  EBML reading and the header before the first Cluster (a CodecPrivate over
  1 MiB refused by name); `container_blocks.rs` the Cluster walk
  (unknown-size Clusters end at the next level-1 element, three lacings,
  payloads skipped, a truncated tail ends the index); `container_codec.rs`
  codec ID → fourcc, the synthesised `vpcC`, the AAC ES_Descriptor, Opus TOC
  counts; `container_timing.rs` raw and grid-snapped video times, decode
  times by the largest reorder, audio in samples less CodecDelay,
  laced-frame times, `required_bytes`, and Vorbis's lead (the first packet's
  count); `container_vorbis.rs` the three Vorbis headers walked to the mode
  table, each packet's count by the overlap rule (spec §11 #228-V), with
  `container_vorbis_setup.rs` the setup header's walk (codebooks, floors,
  residues, mappings, modes); `container.rs` the first video and
  audio track and `describe`/`retime`/`sample_count`/`sample`;
  `ffi_container.rs` the six `rc_container_*` exports. The Colour
  element's MaxCLL, MaxFALL and MasteringMetadata are read too (HD-18):
  `container_codec.rs` writes them as the `mdcv`/`clli` blobs (and reads them
  back, `mastering_from_mdcv` and `light_from_clli`, for the WebM writer) and
  `describe` publishes `mdcv_hex`, `clli_hex`, `transfer`, `primaries`,
  `matrix` and `stream_matrix` (the first VP9 keyframe's `color_space` as a matrix code,
  from `vpcc`; spec §11 CX-16 (10)); the app writes the blobs and the PQ label only for transfer 16. The only payload read
  is the first VP9 keyframe's header, each Opus packet's TOC and each Vorbis
  packet's first byte.
- `ffi_graphic.rs` — the twelve `rc_graphic_*` exports (road map 10 §5e; the
  eleventh `rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39: set the decoded-image cache's
  limit, answer its bytes; the twelfth `rc_graphic_library_usage`, G-46: the
  font files and assets the library's draws used; two re-exported from
  `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`
  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are

  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,

  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,

  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
